title_en: Yuzhong District People's Procuratorate of Chongqing v. Zhu Bowei and Lei Xiuping — robbery case
ruling_gist_en: A taxi driver, during normal operation, for the purpose of obtaining illegal gains, uses violence or threats to forcibly demand from passengers a taxi service fee that is vastly disproportionate to a reasonable price, where the circumstances are serious, such conduct constitutes the crime of forced transactions under Article 226 of the Criminal Law, and shall not be convicted and punished as the crime of robbery.

full_text_en:
Procuratorate of Yuzhong District, Chongqing Municipality v. Zhu Bowei and Lei Xiuping — robbery case

【Ruling Summary】

A taxi driver who, during normal operations, for the purpose of obtaining illegal benefits, uses violence or threats to forcibly collect from a passenger an exorbitant taxi service fee that is vastly different from a reasonable price, and the circumstances are serious, his act constitutes the crime of forced transaction as provided in Article 226 of the Criminal Law, and should not be convicted and punished as robbery.

Procuratorial Authority: Procuratorate of Yuzhong District, Chongqing Municipality.

Defendants:
1. Zhu Bowei, male, 27 years old, native of Chongqing, taxi driver, residing in Changshou District, Chongqing, arrested on October 12, 2005.
2. Lei Xiuping, male, 32 years old, native of Sichuan Province, taxi driver, residing in Yuzhong District, Chongqing, arrested on October 12, 2005.

The Procuratorate of Yuzhong District, Chongqing Municipality instituted a public prosecution with the Yuzhong District People's Court of Chongqing Municipality against the defendants Zhu Bowei and Lei Xiuping for the crime of robbery.

The indictment alleged: While driving a taxi to transport a passenger, defendant Zhu Bowei used verbal threats and body searches to rob passenger Pi Guangsi of RMB 100. Zhu Bowei also, in collusion with defendant Lei Xiuping, used verbal threats and body searches to rob passenger Yang Jianguo of RMB 500. The acts of Zhu Bowei and Lei Xiuping have violated the provisions of Article 263 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Criminal Law), constituting the crime of robbery, and they should be punished according to law.

The prosecutorial authority submitted the following evidence to the court:

1. The report statement of victim Pi Guangsi, the main content of which is: On the evening of September 8, 2005, I got off the train and near Caiyuanba, I boarded a taxi with license plate number Yu BT0735. When I got in, I asked the driver how much it would be to the North Bus Station. The driver said RMB 10. I said nothing, placed my suitcase in the trunk, and sat in the front passenger seat. During the trip, the driver asked if I wanted to stay in a hotel, and said that the hotels are full of bad people, that I must have money, and that I should go to a hotel instead. I refused. After crossing the Jialing River Bridge, the driver said that public security is bad now, that several of his friends are bad people, that he used to be a bad person too, and told me to take out my money. If I did not, he and his friends would kill me and throw me into a ditch, and so on. While driving, he searched my bag and took RMB 100. When we arrived at the North Bus Station, the driver gave me my suitcase and drove away.

2. The report statement of victim Yang Jianguo, the main content of which is: At 12:20 a.m. on September 9, 2005, I was at Chongqing Jiangbei Airport and wanted to go to Caiyuanba. I boarded a taxi with license plate number Yu BT0735 and sat in the back seat. Shortly after we set off, we encountered another taxi at an intersection. The driver of that other taxi said to our driver that he had a passenger who wanted to go to Jiangbei, and asked our driver to take him along. That passenger came over and sat in the front passenger seat. A man also got out of the other taxi, who knew our driver, and he also got into our taxi, sitting next to me. When we arrived in Jiangbei, the passenger who had hitched a ride got out. The man sitting next to me asked me how much the fare from the airport to Caiyuanba usually was. I said RMB 50 during the day, and at most RMB 80 at night. At that point, our driver slammed the steering wheel and cursed: "What the hell, how could it be 50 or 80? I'm working so hard in the middle of the night, pay 480, not a cent less." The man next to me also started searching my bag. I told him not to, but he said viciously: "Take your hand away. If you don't behave, I'll stab you with a knife." In this way, he took RMB 650 from my trouser pocket. When we arrived at Caiyuanba, I said: "Brother, I still need to go back to Guang'an. Give me back some money for the road." At my request, they returned RMB 150 to me.

3. The testimony of witness Zuo Guangying, the main content of which is: Taxi Yu BT0735 is owned by me and was driven by Zhu Bowei. In the early morning of September 9, 2005, Lei Xiuping and I were driving taxi Yu BT2046 back to Chongqing from Guang'an. At the entrance of Chongqing Jiangbei Airport, we met Zhu Bowei. At that time, Zhu Bowei had a passenger in his car, sitting in the back. I asked Zhu Bowei to take the passenger from my car to Mahuangliang in Jiangbei and collect a fare of RMB 40 on my behalf. After that passenger got into Zhu Bowei's car, Lei Xiuping also got into Zhu Bowei's car. When we parted, I told Zhu Bowei and Lei Xiuping not to overcharge. At 1:00 a.m., I called Zhu Bowei, asked where his car was, and also asked how much he had collected from the passenger going to Caiyuanba in Yuzhong District. Zhu Bowei said he had collected RMB 500. I said they were overcharging and that if there were problems, I would not be responsible. Afterwards, Zhu Bowei gave me RMB 300, of which RMB 160 was the operating income Zhu Bowei should have turned over to me, RMB 40 was the fare Zhu Bowei collected for me, and he also gave me an additional RMB 100 as a share.

The defendants Zhu Bowei and Lei Xiuping had no objection to the facts alleged in the indictment, but both argued that they did not have the motive to commit robbery and that their acts did not constitute the crime of robbery.

Defense counsel for the two defendants submitted: The motive for the crime of robbery is greed for money, and the criminal purpose is the illegal possession of public or private property. If the defendants had the motive and purpose to commit robbery, they would not have taken only part of the victims' money and property instead of all of it; if the defendants had the motive and purpose to commit robbery, they would not have returned the suitcase to the first victim or refunded RMB 150 to the second victim for travel expenses back home; if the defendants had the motive and purpose to commit robbery, they would not have used a vehicle with genuine and complete license plates to commit the crime, nor would they have taken the passengers to their destinations after obtaining the money, because doing so would easily expose their true identities and involve great risk. Therefore, the defendants' acts did not meet the constituent elements of the crime of robbery, but rather met the constituent elements of the crime of forced transaction. In addition, the defendants were first-time offenders, had voluntarily surrendered, showed good attitude in admitting guilt, actively returned the stolen money, and did not cause losses to the victims. Counsel suggested a lighter punishment.

The Yuzhong District People's Court of Chongqing Municipality found after trial:

At around 9:00 p.m. on September 8, 2005, defendant Zhu Bowei was driving taxi Yu BT0735 and picked up passenger Pi Guangsi at the Caiyuanba Railway Station to take him to the North Bus Station in Chongqing. During the trip, Zhu Bowei first tried to persuade Pi Guangsi to stay in a hotel. After being refused, he used verbal threats and other means to forcibly take RMB 100 from Pi Guangsi's shirt pocket, and then delivered Pi Guangsi to his destination. In the early morning of the next day, at around 1:00 a.m., Zhu Bowei picked up passenger Yang Jianguo at Jiangbei Airport to take him to Caiyuanba. During the trip, he picked up defendant Lei Xiuping, who also intended to return to Yuzhong District, Chongqing. On the way to Caiyuanba, Zhu Bowei and Lei Xiuping demanded that Yang Jianguo pay a taxi fare of RMB 480. Yang Jianguo refused. Zhu Bowei and Lei Xiuping then verbally threatened Yang Jianguo, and Lei Xiuping forcibly searched Yang Jianguo's body, taking out RMB 650. After delivering Yang Jianguo to his destination, at Yang Jianguo's request, Zhu Bowei and Lei Xiuping returned RMB 150 to Yang Jianguo, forcibly taking the remaining RMB 500. On the 13th and 16th of the same month, Zhu Bowei and Lei Xiuping respectively surrendered to the public security authorities, truthfully confessed the details of the crime, and returned the stolen money of RMB 600.

The above facts are confirmed by the following evidence: the report statements of victims Pi Guangsi and Yang Jianguo, a receipt written by Yang Jianguo, the testimony of witness Zuo Guangying, the motor vehicle driving permit and operating permit, a list of seized and returned items, identification records, and the confessions of the defendants.

The disputed issue in this case is: Do the acts of Zhu Bowei and Lei Xiuping constitute the crime of robbery or the crime of forced transaction?

The Yuzhong District People's Court of Chongqing Municipality held:

Article 263 of the Criminal Law provides: "Whoever robs public or private property by violence, coercion, or other methods shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than ten years, and shall also be fined; under any of the following circumstances, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years, life imprisonment, or death, and shall also be fined or have his property confiscated: (1) robbing a house; (2) robbing on a public means of transportation; (3) robbing a bank or any other financial institution; (4) robbing repeatedly or robbing a huge amount of property; (5) causing serious injury or death in robbery; (6) impersonating a military or police officer to rob; (7) robbing with a firearm; (8) robbing military materials or materials for emergency rescue, disaster relief, or social relief." This is the crime of robbery as stipulated in the Criminal Law. The subject of this crime is any natural person who has reached the age of 14 and has criminal capacity; the object infringed upon is the ownership of public and private property and the personal rights of citizens, and the target of infringement is various properties owned by the state, collectives, or individuals, and the person of others; the subjective aspect is direct intent, with the purpose of illegally possessing public or private property; the objective aspect is the immediate use of violence, coercion, or other methods of physical compulsion against the owner, custodian, or guardian of public or private property on the spot, to immediately take away the property or compel the victim to immediately hand over the property.

Article 226 of the Criminal Law provides: "Whoever, by violence or threats, forces another person to buy or sell commodities, or forces another person to provide or accept services, if the circumstances are serious, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years or criminal detention, and shall also, or shall only, be fined." This is the crime of forced transaction as stipulated in the Criminal Law. The subject of this crime includes not only natural persons but also units; the object infringed upon is the lawful rights and interests of the counterparty to the transaction and the order of the commodity trading market; the subjective aspect is direct intent, with the purpose of conducting a transaction at an unreasonable price or by improper means; the objective aspect is the act of using violence or threats against the counterparty to the transaction, forcing the counterparty to buy or sell commodities, provide or accept services, if the circumstances are serious.

Comparing the two crimes, the prerequisite conditions for the crime are different, the objects infringed upon are different, the purposes are different, and the objective aspects are also somewhat different. Robbery does not require any prerequisite conditions, while forced transaction must involve a transaction between the perpetrator and the victim; the object infringed upon by robbery is the ownership of public and private property and the personal rights of citizens, while the object infringed upon by forced transaction is the lawful rights and interests of the counterparty to the transaction and the order of the commodity trading market; the purpose of robbery is to illegally possess public or private property, while the purpose of forced transaction is to conduct a transaction at an unreasonable price or by improper means; although both crimes involve violence and coercion in their objective aspects, due to the different objects infringed upon, the violence and coercion used in robbery are generally sufficient to endanger the victim's health or life safety, and their intensity is greater than the violence and threats used in forced transaction.

The defendants Zhu Bowei and Lei Xiuping were both taxi drivers, and the victims Pi Guangsi and Yang Jianguo were both taxi passengers. Between Zhu Bowei and Pi Guangsi and Yang Jianguo, a transactional relationship of providing and receiving services was established, and it was because of this relationship that they met. During Zhu Bowei's operation, Lei Xiuping joined Zhu Bowei, knowing that Zhu Bowei was providing services to a passenger. In the process of Zhu Bowei providing services to the passengers, Zhu Bowei and Lei Xiuping used violence and threats to forcibly take money from Pi Guangsi and Yang Jianguo. On the surface, the methods used by Zhu Bowei and Lei Xiuping were no different from robbery. However, the violence and threats used by Zhu Bowei and Lei Xiuping were not sufficient to endanger the victims' health or life safety. Considering the circumstances that the two defendants used a vehicle with genuine and complete license plates to commit the crime, delivered the passengers to their destinations after committing the crime, voluntarily returned the suitcase to the passenger at the destination, and returned a portion of the money to the passenger, it is analyzed that Zhu Bowei and Lei Xiuping did not have the purpose of illegally possessing public or private property, but rather aimed to complete a transaction at an unreasonable price. Therefore, the acts of Zhu Bowei and Lei Xiuping do not meet the constituent elements of the crime of robbery, but constitute forced transaction. Zhu Bowei and Lei Xiuping, as taxi drivers, for the purpose of obtaining illegal benefits, defied the law, and during normal taxi operations, against the will of the victims, individually or jointly used violence or threats to forcibly collect exorbitant taxi service fees that were vastly different from reasonable prices, seriously infringing upon the lawful rights and interests of the counterparties to the transactions and the order of the taxi market. The forced transaction was serious, and their acts violated the provisions of Article 226 of the Criminal Law, constituting the crime of forced transaction.

In summary, the defenses and arguments of the defendants Zhu Bowei and Lei Xiuping and their defense counsel that their acts did not constitute the crime of robbery are established and should be adopted. The facts alleged in the indictment are clear, and the evidence is reliable and sufficient, but the charge alleged is incorrect and should be corrected. After the incident, Zhu Bowei and Lei Xiuping voluntarily surrendered to the public security authorities and truthfully confessed their criminal facts. Although they later retracted their confessions, they corrected themselves before the judgment was pronounced, which still constitutes voluntary surrender. They also fully returned the stolen money. Accordingly, they may be given a lighter punishment according to law. Pursuant to this, the Yuzhong District People's Court of Chongqing Municipality rendered the following judgment on January 27, 2006:

1. Defendant Zhu Bowei is guilty of the crime of forced transaction and is sentenced to ten months' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 2,000;
2. Defendant Lei Xiuping is guilty of the crime of forced transaction and is sentenced to six months' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 2,000.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, the defendants Zhu Bowei and Lei Xiuping did not appeal within the statutory period, and the prosecutorial authority did not protest. The first-instance judgment became legally effective.
